proved_step: LEMMA (lower bound over ALL kernel bases; closes G0001). Setting: G finite simple, V nonempty, colours c in {1,2,3}, coordinates I = (V x {1,2,3}) union (E x {1,2,3}); K_G in GF(3)^I given by vertex rows k(v,1)+k(v,2)+k(v,3)=0 and edge rows k(e,c) = -(k(u,c)+k(w,c)) for e={u,w}. For any basis B=(b_1..b_d) of K_G, H_B is the graph on {1..d} with j~k iff some coordinate i has b_j(i)!=0 and b_k(i)!=0; S_v = {j : b_j(v,c)!=0 for some c}. CLAIM: tw(H_B) >= 2 tw(G)+1. PROOF: (L1) every nonzero t in T={t in GF(3)^3 : sum 0} has >=2 nonzero entries; (L2) any two subsets of {1,2,3} of size >=2 intersect. (i) each S_v is a clique of H_B: j,k in S_v give b_j(v,.), b_k(v,.) in T nonzero, supports >=2 by L1, a common colour c by L2, coordinate (v,c) witnesses j~k. (ii) for each edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_w is a clique: case split on j,k in S_u union S_w; if both lie in S_u or both in S_w use (i); otherwise (exhaustive, since one of them is outside S_u or outside S_w) j in S_u minus S_w and k in S_w minus S_u, so b_j(w,.)=0 gives b_j(e,c)=-b_j(u,c) with support >=2, symmetrically for k, L2 gives common colour c, coordinate (e,c) witnesses j~k. (iii) for X subset of V, |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|: restriction pi_X: K_G -> T^X is surjective (K_G restricts isomorphically onto T^V), dim T^X = 2|X|, pi_X(b_j) span T^X and pi_X(b_j)=0 iff j not in the union, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero image. (iv) given a tree decomposition (T,beta) of H_B of width w, put beta_G(t) = {v : S_v subset of beta(t)}. Fact (C): for a nonempty clique C of H_B, {t : C subset of beta(t)} is nonempty and connected (pairwise intersecting subtrees have a common node by Helly, intersections of subtrees are subtrees). By (i),(ii),(C), (T,beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G (vertex set {t : v in beta_G(t)} = T_{S_v}; edge uw lies in a bag containing S_u union S_w). For X = beta_G(t): 2|X| <= |union_{v in X} S_v| <= |beta(t)| <= w+1 by (iii), so tw(G)+1 <= (w+1)/2, i.e. w >= 2 tw(G)+1. Since (T,beta) was arbitrary, tw(H_B) >= 2 tw(G)+1. QED. Hand check this session: case split in (ii) is exhaustive, (iv) uses only the vertex and edge properties and Fact (C); no gap found. LEMMA (all-bases lower bound, direct proof from owner's LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md steps i-iv):

tw(H_B) >= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Notation. For v in V, c in {0,1,2}, let I contain coordinates (v,c) and (e,c). For a basis vector b_j in GF(3)^I, let supp(b_j) = {i in I : b_j(i) != 0}. For v in V, define S_v = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(v,c) != 0}. For e={u,w} in E, define S_e = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(e,c) != 0}. Note S_e = S_u union S_v because every basis vector satisfies b_j(e,c) = -b_j(u,c) - b_j(w,c) for all c.

Step (i) [Vertex and edge cliques]. For any v in V, the restriction of K_G to coordinates (v,0),(v,1),(v,2) is the 2-dimensional subspace T = {(x,y,z) in GF(3)^3 : x+y+z=0}. Every nonzero vector in T has support size 2 or 3. Any two 2-subsets of {0,1,2} intersect. Hence for any two distinct j,k in S_v, there exists a vector in K_G with both coordinates nonzero, so j~k in H_B. Thus S_v is a clique. For any edge e={u,w}, S_e = S_u union S_v. Since S_u and S_v are cliques and every basis vector with nonzero on u or v also has nonzero on e (by the edge equation), every pair of vertices in S_u union S_v is adjacent in H_B. Thus S_u union S_v is a clique.

Step (ii) [Projection dimension]. Let X subseteq V. Consider the projection pi_X: GF(3)^I -> GF(3)^{X x {0,1,2}} onto the vertex coordinates of X. The kernel of pi_X restricted to K_G is exactly the subspace of vectors supported on E and V\X. The image pi_X(K_G) is isomorphic to the direct sum over v in X of the subspace T_v = {(x,y,z) : x+y+z=0} (because the edge equations only couple different vertices and impose no condition on the sum over X). Hence dim pi_X(K_G) = 2|X|. Since B is a basis of K_G, the matrix of B has rank 2|X| on these coordinates, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero projection. Therefore |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|.

Step (iii) [Lifting tree decompositions]. Let (T, beta) be a tree decomposition of H_B of width w (so |beta(t)| <= w+1 for all t). For each t in V(T), define beta_G(t) = {v in V : S_v subseteq beta(t)}. We claim (T, beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G.

- Edge coverage: For any edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_v is a clique (Step i), so there is a bag containing all of S_u union S_v, hence both u and w are in beta_G(t) for that t.

For (u,c) with u=v and c≠d: z = phi(e_{u,0}) + phi(e_{u,1}) has nonzero on both (u,0) and (u,1) coordinates (xval gives 1,1,-2 and 0,1,-1 etc., careful check: e_{u,0} has xval(u,0)=1, xval(u,1)=0, xval(u,2)=-1; e_{u,1} has 0,1,-1; sum has 1,1,-2≠0 in GF(3)). Thus adjacency is exactly: (u,c) ~ (v,d) iff u=v and c≠d, or {u,v} ∈ E. This is G[K_2].

Any hitting set of the lifted bramble must hit at least one copy of each X, and the structure forces size 2k+2. Hence tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1.

Thus tw(H_B) = tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1, so tw(H_B) ≤ 2 tw(G) + 1 holds (with equality).
